description:
Staff Software Engineer, AI-Native Systems

Location: Remote (US)

We are

Virtual care only works if the infrastructure behind it does. Wheel builds that infrastructure: the systems that let telehealth run at scale for the patients, clinicians, and companies that depend on it. We're not bolting AI onto old workflows; we're rebuilding how care gets delivered, with AI in the product and in how we build it.

We do this in a live, regulated healthcare environment where getting it right matters. This is the next architecture of virtual care, and we're building it now.

You are

A staff-level engineer who has built software in a regulated, high-stakes domain (ideally health tech; fintech and insurtech count too) and knows what that demands: sensitive data, regulatory constraints, and the cost of getting it wrong. You've designed and shipped AI and agentic systems in production, you know where they break, and you have opinions, held loosely and argued well, about building them safely.

You're a builder first, and you've done real work in small, scrappy teams. You still write the hard parts of the code yourself, and you've done it recently. You don't need a platform org, TPMs, or layers of review to move.

You operate as a domain owner, not a task owner. You take a problem that isn't well-formed, define it, tie it to what the business has committed to, and lead a group of engineers to a shipped, measured outcome. Your impact shows up in other people's work: the patterns they reuse and the ambiguity you removed before it cost the team a quarter.

You get things done. You have sharp judgment about what actually moves the outcome, you'd rather ship something useful this week than something perfect next quarter, and you know when good enough is good enough (and when, in healthcare, it isn't).

And you're good to work with. You're curious, generous with your time, quick to give credit, and you can disagree hard without making it personal. Smart matters here; kind matters just as much. Bonus points if people genuinely enjoy being on a team with you.

The Work

Technical Leadership & Direction

  • Own the technical direction for a significant AI-native area of the platform, such as patient and clinician experiences, care delivery, or the AI platform layer other teams build on.

  • Act as tech lead for a team or cross-team initiative: break down ambiguous problems, sequence delivery, clear blockers, and keep the team pointed at the outcome rather than the ticket.

  • Connect day-to-day engineering to quarterly commitments and company goals, and make those links visible to the team.

  • Write and review design docs. Make and document the load-bearing calls, including "not yet" and "buy, don't build."

AI & Agent Engineering

  • Design and build production AI features and agents: retrieval, orchestration, tool calling, guardrails, evaluation, and observability.

  • Define what "production-ready" means for AI here (testability, rollback safety, cost ceilings, failure modes, human-in-the-loop boundaries) and hold the bar in review.

  • Take on the hardest parts of the build yourself. This is a hands-on role; you are expected to be in the code every day.

Healthcare-Grade Engineering

  • Treat privacy, security, and responsible AI use on sensitive health data as hard engineering requirements, and turn compliance constraints into concrete architecture.

  • Partner with clinical, compliance, and legal stakeholders early, so safety and review are designed in rather than bolted on.

  • Build for the realities of healthcare: integrations with clinical systems, auditability, and high-reliability workflows.

Cloud-Native Delivery

  • Own full-stack delivery in TypeScript/Node.js and Python: services, APIs, data jobs, and the interfaces on top.

  • Own deployment, monitoring, and troubleshooting in production, including on-call, and improve the operational posture of what you inherit.

Measure & Improve

  • Own the evaluation strategy for your area: metrics, test harnesses, and plans for accuracy, latency, safety, and cost.

  • Instrument systems so their behavior is legible after the fact, not just at demo time.

  • Kill approaches that aren't working, early and visibly.

Stakeholders & The Org

  • Work directly with product, operations, clinical, and business leaders to decide which use cases are worth building.

  • Explain trade-offs and risks clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, up to the executive team.

  • Mentor engineers through code review, design review, and pairing, and build reusable patterns that raise the bar beyond your own team.

What success looks like

  • First 30 days: you've shipped something to production, met the people you'll build with, and know where the sharp edges are.

  • First 90 days: you own an area, set its technical direction, and have shipped AI features with an evaluation story behind them.

  • First 6 months: patterns you established are used by teams you don't sit on, the business can point to outcomes you drove, and engineers say their work got better (and more fun) because you're here.

What we're looking for

  • 8+ years building and operating production software, with full-stack depth in TypeScript/Node.js and at least one other language (Python strongly preferred).

  • 3+ years building software in health tech, fintech, or insurtech, including work with sensitive data under HIPAA, PCI, SOC 2, or similar requirements.

  • Hands-on experience designing and shipping AI or agentic systems in production (retrieval, orchestration, tool calling, evaluation), with a clear view of where LLMs work and where they don't.

  • A record of shipping outcomes, not just output: you can point to what you delivered, why it mattered, and the judgment calls you made to get it out the door.

  • Recent hands-on output: in the last two years you've personally built and debugged significant production systems, not only directed others.

  • Meaningful time at a startup or growth-stage company where you owned what platform, release, or infrastructure teams would handle elsewhere.

  • A track record of technical leadership as an IC: owning a domain, leading multi-engineer efforts to completion, and driving decisions across teams without positional authority.

  • A collaborative, low-ego style: you raise the people around you and make hard conversations easier, not harder.

  • Fluent use of AI development tools as a force multiplier, with judgment about when to trust, verify, or override them.

  • Strong cloud-native fundamentals: CI/CD, observability, and running what you build. Fluency with relational data and SQL.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, including design docs that change minds. This is a remote, cross-functional role.

Strongly desired

  • Health tech experience specifically: telehealth, EHR/EMR, digital health, payer/provider, or pharmacy.

  • Experience with clinical workflows or integrations with clinical systems (EHRs, e-prescribing, labs, HL7/FHIR).

  • Model evaluation and guardrail infrastructure: measuring output quality, catching regressions, and keeping AI inside safe bounds.

  • Patient-, clinician-, or customer-facing AI products shipped to real users.

  • Experience building platform capabilities consumed by other engineering teams.

  • Experience as a formal tech lead or mentoring engineers.

What's hard about this role

We'd rather you hear it now:

  • Ambiguity is the job. Problems often arrive half-formed, and priorities can shift as the business and market change.

  • You'll build, not just direct. There's no large platform org; you'll write code, run what you ship, and take on-call.

  • Healthcare raises the bar. Clinical safety, privacy, and compliance review are part of shipping, and they take real time.

If that sounds energizing rather than draining, we'd love to talk.

How we work

Remote-first (US), fast-moving, with tight loops between engineering, product, clinical, and the business. We're an AI-forward engineering org: we expect AI in the toolchain and in the product, and we measure outcomes over activity. We handle sensitive healthcare data under strict controls; privacy, security, and responsible AI are engineering requirements, not afterthoughts.

We take the work seriously, not ourselves. We're direct and kind, we help each other out, and we have fun doing it.

 
 

Salary and Perks

Pay Range: $185,725-$264,500 USD

Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including, but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the role, the selected candidate’s work experience, education and training, the work location as well as market and business considerations.

 

As an employee of Wheel, you’ll enjoy our Total Rewards Program to help secure your financial future and preserve your health and well-being, including:

  • Medical, Dental and Vision

  • Ancillary: Life, Short and Long Term Disability

  • 401K match

  • Flexible PTO

  • Parental Leave

  • Stock options

  • Additional programs and perks

Wheel is committed to equal employment opportunities for all team members. Every decision we make regarding employment is solely based on merit, competence, and performance. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.

Research shows that underrepresented groups typically apply only if they meet 100% of the criteria listed. At Wheel, we encourage women, people of color, and LGBTQ+ job seekers to apply for positions even if they don’t check every box for the role.
